data.narrative:
Augury, a Series F robotics and manufacturing diagnostics company founded by Gal Shaul and Saar Yoskovitz, has raised $369M to date. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector comprises 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though a narrow peer set at Augury's stage and tier is limited to fewer than three datapoints, constraining traditional multiples-based approaches.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable lens. Using total capital raised ($369M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.3x step-up multiplier typical of Series F progression yields an implied valuation of $480M. This single-method triangulation limits precision; the 15% sensitivity band around this estimate ($408M–$552M) reflects inherent uncertainty in single-method reliance rather than cross-validation across independent approaches.

The valuation range of $408M–$552M (median $480M) is supportable on stage mechanics alone, but material uncertainty remains. A peer-median method could not be reliably applied due to insufficient same-stage or tier-matched comparables in the robotics sector. Key uncertainties include burn rate relative to raised capital, gross margins and unit economics in installed base, and velocity of enterprise adoption in manufacturing. Additional datapoints on recent Series F rounds in adjacent automation subsectors or manufacturing software would strengthen conviction in this range.
